title: HCLTech Commits $1.5 Billion to Build India's First Sovereign AI Data Centre in Odisha
excerpt: The IT giant partners with Sarvam AI and the Odisha government to set up a full-stack AI facility at the state's new Sovereign AI Park, alongside a 5,000-person technology centre.
body:
• HCLTech will invest ₹14,257 crore ($1.48 billion) to build its first AI data centre at the upcoming Odisha Sovereign AI Park in Bhubaneswar.
  • The project is a three-way partnership between HCLTech, AI startup Sarvam, and the Odisha state government, backed by state financial assistance.
  • A separate Global Technology Centre in Bhubaneswar will employ 5,000 people and begin operations by 2028.
  • The facility will combine HCLTech's infrastructure with Sarvam's foundation models to deliver multilingual, sector-specific AI applications.

A $1.5 Billion Bet on Sovereign AI

HCLTech on Friday announced plans to invest ₹14,257 crore ($1.48 billion) in its first artificial intelligence data centre, to be built at the upcoming Odisha Sovereign AI Park in Bhubaneswar. The project, formalized through a memorandum of understanding with the Odisha state government and AI startup Sarvam, is one of the largest single investments in India's sovereign AI infrastructure to date.

The investment includes financial assistance from the state government, though neither side disclosed the split. The data centre will combine HCLTech's full-stack AI capabilities — spanning infrastructure, compute, models and applications — with Sarvam's domestically developed foundation models to build sector-specific AI tools for both private and public enterprises.

India's Sovereign AI Ambitions Take Shape

The deal arrives as India pushes to reduce its dependence on foreign AI platforms and build homegrown alternatives. Sarvam, which completed a $234 million first close on its $300 million Series B round at a $1.5 billion valuation in June, has positioned itself as a builder of the full AI stack — from training and inference infrastructure to frontier model research and enterprise deployment.

HCLTech had already invested $150 million for a 10.46% stake in Sarvam last month, signaling the depth of the strategic alignment between the two companies.

"HCLTech has been a flag bearer of India's technology industry. We strive to be an enabler of India's sovereign AI ecosystem with differentiated offerings across the value chain through focused investments and partnerships."

— Roshni Nadar Malhotra, Chairperson, HCLTech

5,000 Jobs and a New Tech Hub

Alongside the data centre, HCLTech will set up a separate Global Technology Centre in Bhubaneswar. The facility will house 5,000 employees and is expected to start operations by 2028. Both projects were formalized through MOUs signed in the presence of Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and state IT Minister Mukesh Mahaling.

CEO C. Vijayakumar called the project "an important milestone" in HCLTech's full-stack AI strategy, citing Odisha's progressive policy environment and infrastructure. The company currently employs 1.7 lakh people across technology campuses in Noida, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune and several other Indian cities.

A Growing Race Among Indian IT Giants

The announcement places HCLTech in direct competition with larger rival Tata Consultancy Services, which committed $2 billion last November to develop AI data centres in partnership with private equity firm TPG. The AI boom has triggered a rush among Indian IT firms to build data centre capacity, with India seen as a key market due to its massive internet user base and comparatively lower power and operating costs.

Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said the Odisha facility will "connect high-performance compute with Indian models and real-world applications" at scale. The company's models are designed to support multilingual AI services, a critical requirement in a country with 22 official languages.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs working in tech, the investment signals that India's AI ecosystem is maturing beyond services and outsourcing into deep infrastructure. The sovereign AI push — designed to keep Indian data on Indian soil and process it with Indian-built models — could create new career pathways for diaspora technologists considering a return.
